definitions: Carl Menger (1840-1921) was an Austrian economist and the founder of the Austrian School of economics. He is known for his contributions to the development of marginal utility theory and his methodological individualism.

Carl Menger was an influential figure in the history of economic thought, whose work laid the groundwork for the subjective theory of value and the understanding of economic phenomena as emerging from individual actions.
examples: Carl Menger's Principles of Economics is a foundational text in the Austrian School.
Students of economic history often study Carl Menger's contributions to marginal utility theory.
The ideas of Carl Menger continue to influence contemporary economic discussions.
